projects.name: Data-Man
projects.subtitle: Your data. A better conversation.
projects.description: An agentic assistant that turns natural-language questions into schema-aware SQL analysis and data transformations.
projects.contribution: I engineered the SQL and ETL agent workflow, schema-aware retrieval, and JEV routing and evaluation.
projects.problem: Asking a question about a database can require understanding its schema, writing SQL, and preparing the result for analysis. Data-Man explores how natural-language interaction can connect these steps.
projects.solution: An agentic workflow coordinates SQL analysis and ETL agents. Schema-aware RAG retrieves relevant table and column context for SQL generation. TypeSafeAI JEV supports tool-call selection, guardrail enforcement, and evaluation of routing, execution, and response quality.
contributions: Engineered a workflow coordinating SQL analysis and ETL agents for natural-language database queries and transformation requests.
Implemented schema-aware RAG to retrieve relevant table and column context for SQL generation.
Integrated TypeSafeAI JEV for tool-call selection, guardrails, and evaluation of routing decisions, tool execution, and response quality.
considerations: Schema context helps ground SQL generation, while retrieval relevance remains an important evaluation target.
Coordinating specialized tools introduces routing decisions that need guardrails and evaluation alongside answer quality.
projects.outcome: An implemented natural-language workflow for PostgreSQL queries and requested data transformations. No quantitative benchmark is supplied.

projects.name: LLM Inference Placement
projects.subtitle: The right request. The right GPU.
projects.description: Ongoing research into placing LLM requests across heterogeneous GPU tiers using output-length prediction and load-aware scheduling.
projects.contribution: I am developing the placement layer and evaluating latency, financial cost, and energy across workloads.
projects.problem: LLM requests have different compute needs. Serving them across heterogeneous GPUs raises questions about how to balance latency requirements, financial cost, and energy consumption.
projects.solution: I am developing an LLM inference placement layer that routes requests across heterogeneous GPU tiers. Output-length prediction and load-aware scheduling guide placement with the goal of reducing cost while meeting latency SLOs.
contributions: Developing an inference placement layer for heterogeneous GPU tiers.
Using output-length prediction and load-aware scheduling to guide routing decisions.
Evaluating tier-aware placement against single-tier and First-Come, First-Served baselines using vLLM, measuring latency, financial cost, and energy consumption.
considerations: Lower-cost placement must be balanced against latency SLOs and the uncertainty of output-length estimates.
Single-tier and FCFS baselines provide reference points for evaluating tier-aware scheduling across workloads.
projects.outcome: Research in progress. Latency, cost, and energy are evaluation targets; completed performance results are not yet reported.
